Orsted AS Delivers Steady Growth in Renewables Despite Market Headwinds

Danish renewables leader Orsted AS reported a resilient financial performance for the first quarter, underlining steady growth in its core wind and solar businesses despite challenging market conditions. The company posted revenue of DKK 18.4 billion, up 6% compared with the year-earlier period, while operating profit (EBITDA) reached DKK 6.2 billion, in line with analyst expectations.

The company's offshore wind segment continued to drive results, accounting for nearly 60% of total earnings. Orsted AS commissioned two new offshore wind farms in the North Sea during the quarter, adding 0.8 GW of capacity to its portfolio. “Our continued investment in offshore wind demonstrates our commitment to a decarbonized energy future,” said Mads Nipper, CEO of Orsted AS. “Despite inflationary pressures and supply chain volatility, we have maintained strong project delivery and upheld our financial targets.”

The onshore segment also showed progress, with the completion of a 200 MW solar project in Jutland. The company reported that its total installed renewable capacity has now reached 16.5 GW, keeping it on track to meet its 2030 goal of 50 GW.

Industry analysts welcomed the results as a sign of stability. “Orsted’s disciplined approach to capital allocation and risk management is paying off in a turbulent market,” said Mette Lund, senior analyst at Nordic Energy Insights. “They remain the benchmark for large-scale renewable operators in Europe.”

The Danish Wind Industry Association noted that Orsted’s performance reflects the broader resilience of the sector, even as high interest rates and regulatory uncertainty weigh on some projects. “Orsted’s results show that Denmark remains at the forefront of clean energy innovation,” said association spokesperson Peter Holm.

Looking ahead, Orsted AS reaffirmed its full-year EBITDA guidance in the range of DKK 20-23 billion, citing a robust project pipeline and steady demand for renewable energy solutions from both public and private sector clients.
